To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• The e‐marketplace model used in Western Australia has the potential to bridge the digital divide, but only if it is implemented in a way that addresses the needs of the SMEs that are to be the primary beneficiaries of the e‐ marketplace.
e‐marketplaces can bridge the digital divide if they are well designed and implemented.
E‐marketplace development has to be a collaborative effort between the government, business and the community.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of e‐marketplaces and the role they play in bridging the digital divide.
the development of e‐marketplaces in Western Australia and the impact of government sponsored e‐markets on the digital divide.
the role of the e‐business intermediary and its impact on the digital divide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the development and implementation of e‐marketplaces is a difficult task.
government sponsored e‐markets are not an effective channel for the development of SMEs in regional areas.
e‐marketplaces have the potential to bridge the digital divide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of e‐marketplaces is a complex process and the outcomes are not guaranteed.
e‐marketplaces, if they are to succeed, must be seen as part of a larger strategy to improve SME participation in the digital economy.
government sponsored e‐markets are a good thing but not if the focus is too narrow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the government should not be the sole driver for an e‐marketplace.
government agencies should not assume that the creation of an e‐marketplace is sufficient to address the needs of small businesses.
government sponsored marketplaces should be more than just a platform to buy and sell products and services.
